articleTitle: Stability Analysis of an Active Mechanical Motion Rectifier for Wave Energy Conversion Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Recent literature proposes a novel Active Mechanical Motion Rectifier (AMMR) based power take-off system. The primary objective of mechanical rectification in wave energy conversion schemes is to ensure controlled unidirectional rotation speed in the generator, aiming to mitigate losses caused by low rotational speed and enhance overall system efficiency. Despite the promising potential of this proposal, ensuring the stability and controllability of the entire system remains an unresolved challenge. In that regard, this work addresses the former issue by providing a preliminary assessment of the stability of a flap operating with the proposed AMMR-based power take-off. The studies conducted in this work set the fundamental basis to facilitate the design of an effective controller for this novel power take-off system. The obtained results are validated through in-silico evaluations, modelling the system as piecewise linear.

articleTitle: Artificial Vision System for Detecting Variations in the Length of Pieces on a Production Line
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Currently, inspecting parts on production lines is a necessary task in many cases, as these parts typically come from machining operations where precision in shape and measurements is crucial to complete the assembly process. In another scenario, after assembly, parts may require a specific position for the next operation. Manual inspection is slow, and efficiency is low. To overcome this issue, the non-contact defect detection process using artificial vision techniques is applicable to these scenarios. The development emerged as a specific need in an industry that required replacing manual inspection with non-contact and automatic inspection on a parts conveyor line, specifically, assembled shock absorbers for heavy vehicles. It is essential for these elements to be fully extended before entering the painting process to avoid areas of the part being without paint coating. A real-time measurement technique was proposed, using standard high-definition web cameras placed in fixed positions, processing the images through edge detection, dilation, and erosion algorithms to estimate the length of the inspected piece and comparing it with the reference model. For this development, two FHD web cameras, a CPU with a monitor and keyboard, a Siemens Logo PLC, and automation elements were used. In terms of software, an application was developed in Python, utilizing the OpenCV library [1] for artificial vision algorithms and the Snap7 library [2] for PLC control and input/output handling for automation logic. Experimental results showed that the piece's length can be estimated using the implemented algorithm, achieving values within the necessary precision on the production line, thus effectively conducting the inspection.

articleTitle: Analysis of Input-Series Output-Series Connected Modular Dual Active Bridge Converter for Medium Voltage DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the input-series output-series (ISOS) connection of dual active bridges (DAB) modules for medium voltage DC microgrids using both centralized and distributed modulators. As a result of this analysis, the voltage distribution between the modules, the soft-switching conditions, and the transferred power as a function of the main design converter parameters are obtained. Finally, experimental results for operation during steady state are presented to validate the analysis.

articleTitle: An Online Short-Circuit Impedance Estimation Approach to Power Transformer Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In addition to offline testing in transformers, advanced diagnostic techniques are experiencing significant advancements in on-line monitoring to ensure the continuity of electrical service and to minimize the costs associated with equipment repair and replacement. This paper presents a strategy for incipient fault detection in power transformers through online measurement of winding impedances. The strategy is based on calculating the series impedance for each phase, which includes the transformer and the connected equipment, by measuring the electrical variables of the transformer. Finally, a single fault indicator is obtained that provides information on the fault severity and the phase affected. The strategy is tested by finite element method simulations for different load conditions and fault severities. The strategy is validated with laboratory results on a 10 kVA three-phase transformer. The results obtained show the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in detecting faults in power transformers.

articleTitle: Changes in Land Covers in Two River Basins in Central Argentina Region. Monitoring the SDG 15.3.1 Indicator
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This study provides an insightful analysis of land cover changes in two river basins in the central Argentina region and is focuses on monitoring the SDG 15.3.1 indicator and highlights the impacts of human and natural forces on land cover patterns at different scales. We analyze land cover transitions in seven land cover classes, at both basin and riverine scales, between the 1992–2015 period on the Suquía and Xanaes water- sheds. Land cover changes observed in this area were related mainly to the increase of artificial land covers, which indicates the possible increase of human impacts in this area, particularly a streamside scales. The paper highlights the relationship between land cover and water quality, particularly in the Suquia River, where urban and agricultural land covers pose a threat to the quality of resources. Urgent action is needed to mitigate human impacts, and an approach to managing riparian areas for better ecosystem maintenance and preservation is proposed. Aligned with SDG 15, our findings are relevant for sustainable resource management and provide essential insights for informed decision-making for the benefit of both the population and the environment.

articleTitle: Impact evaluation of the use of geospatial information for firefighting in Argentina
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: The World Conservation Organization (WWF), revealed in its 2020 report, that the number of fire alerts increased by 13% compared to the previous year, which had already been a record period for fires in South America and the world. Every year countless fires occur throughout Argentina, causing huge losses in different productive sectors and irreparable environmental damage in the short term. In Argentina, there is no operational fire simulation model based on spatial information, which allows improving management and thus reducing damages, ensuring the safety of fire fighters and protecting the ecosystem. This work proposes an evaluation of the socioeconomic benefit of the potential use of an operational simulator for fire management. In this way, by implementing an instrument that allows predicting fire behavior, we seek to increase the social profitability of the policies assigned to different jurisdictional levels in Argentina, allowing better management of prevention, monitoring and recovery of damages associated with future fires.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of the Prototype of a Robotic Platform for Ankle Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper presents the processes of design, construction and control of the prototype of a parallel robot, based on a Stewart platform, in order to be implemented in passive ankle rehabilitation. Its design is achieved by means of computer-aided design software, carrying out its construction through additive 3D printing, rotational actuators and standardized elements. The control is carried out through a graphical user interface programmed in integrated development software and implemented in a microcontroller. Based on the analysis of inverse kinematics, the set allows you to choose to perform the six basic movements for the ankle rehabilitation process: Dorsiflexion, Plantarflexion, Inversion, Eversion, Abduction and Adduction.

articleTitle: Position and velocity determination of people aimed at study of evacuations
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This study describes the application of algorithms on video sequences with the purpose of detecting and identifying individuals moving in crowds (even with occasional occlusions), calculating their position, speed, and trajectory. To achieve this, the YOLO neural network was utilized for people detection, and the ORB descriptor was used for their tracking. Additionally, a Kalman filter was employed to estimate the position and velocity of each detected person. This configuration was applied to various videos, achieving excellent results in terms of the number of people detected and the accuracy in determining the variables. The obtained outcomes are comparable in precision and processing times to those sought in the development of an automated control system applied to people circulation.

articleTitle: Shielding of Electromagnetic Waves at Microwave Frequencies with the Split-Ring Resonator Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work, the shielding efficiency of a split ring resonator (SRR) formed by a periodic structure built from concentric copper rings printed on a dielectric material has been studied. These artificial materials called metamaterials can be represented as a homogeneous material that has effective constitutive parameters that could not be obtained from naturally occurring materials, such as magnetic permeability and electrical permittivity simultaneously negative. Simulations of the effective magnetic permeability of the material were performed by varying the geometry of the metamaterial. This analysis enables the design and construction of structures with properties that make them an attractive candidate for shielding applications in the range of microwave frequencies. This material is an alternative to massive metallic materials and can lower costs in electromagnetic absorbers. The metamaterial has been built with 100 unit cells on each dielectric slab, stacking 5 slabs. We have made experimental measurements of the shielding effectiveness of these materials when subjected to an electromagnetic plane wave with an magnetic field polarized in the direction perpendicular to the dielectric slabs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Applied to Anomaly Detection in Electric Motors Aimed at Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work, we propose an anomaly detector for electric motors based on an Autoencoder implemented on a lowcost, computationally efficient platform. The model was trained on a dataset of 1,225 normal vibration signals, augmented with Gaussian noise. Through topological optimization using genetic algorithms, a compact Autoencoder with 10,336 parameters was obtained, achieving average sensitivity and specificity above 80% for anomaly detection. The model can operate in realtime (reaching 1,990 μs per inference), classifying normal and anomalous vibration signals captured by an accelerometer based on microelectromechanical systems technology. The results demonstrate the feasibility of employing machine learning for cost-effective, in-situ predictive maintenance in electric motors. As future work, the implementation and validation of a complete online system are proposed, along with the development of adaptive methods to establish dynamic thresholds between normal and anomalous states.

articleTitle: Dynamic Eccentricity Detection in Induction Motors using Stator Pole Flux
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work, a strategy for detecting dynamic eccentricity in induction motors based on the flux linked by the stator poles is presented. To achieve this, the effects of eccentricity on magnetic flux are analyzed both analytically and using a finite element model. From this analysis, a residual signal obtained from the difference between the magnetic flux of opposite poles is proposed, which allows the decoupling of the diagnostic signal from the fundamental component. This approach offers an effective alternative for detecting dynamic eccentricity in induction motors. The strategy is validated through laboratory experimental tests on a motor with different levels of eccentricity and independent access to the windings of each pole. The obtained results indicate that it is possible to detect and quantify the eccentricity level in the air-gap based on the flux linked by the windings of a phase.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Control Mechanisms for the Free Trade Fairs of Misiones
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: The objective of this work is to present the general procedure that emerges from an organizational strategic management model developed to improve the operating conditions of the Free Trade Fairs in the province of Misiones, and to analyze the main control mechanisms established in the different stages. As the main result of this investigation, the proposed general procedure is endowed with several control mechanisms in the different phases and stages, for the most part, they are simple and specific for the purposes for which they were designed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Sliding-Mode Controller for a DC-DC Boost-buck Converter Feeding a Generalized Load
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper presents the model and design of a sliding mode controller for a boost buck DC-DC converter operating in continuous conduction mode (CCM). The converter supplies a generalized power load consisting of a resistive component, a current source, and a constant power load. The control strategy is designed based on a nonlinear energy-based system output. It also includes a linear disturbance observer for load current estimation. Simulation results with reference and load variations are provided for design validation.

articleTitle: Crop monitoring with L-Band Vegetation Optical Depth (VOD): investigation in southeastern of Argentine Pampas
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This study presents an initial investigation into crop (barley and soybean) monitoring using vegetation optical depth (VOD) retrieved from the NASA Soil Moisture Active Passive mission (SMAP). VOD was consistent with Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and latent heat flux (LE) from Moderate-Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) within the southeastern area of the Argentine Pampas. Pre-liminary results reveal the potential of L-band VOD as a tool for monitoring water crops condition, demonstrating relevant synergies with traditional vegetation indicators.

articleTitle: Distributed Generation Insertion in Electrical Networks: A Case Study in Misiones, Argentina
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This work presents a methodology applied to electrical distribution systems considering the Distributed Generation (DG) insertion in Misiones, Argentina. The proposed study aims to determine the maximum penetration level of DG in several distribution networks, without exceeding the technical quality limits specified by current regulations. First, the 13.2 kV distribution networks were modeled in the PowerFactory power system analysis software. Based on the radial standard network operation, different procedures and criteria for the location and sizing of the DG in all electrical nodes were proposed. The results show that for long feeders, the maximum insertion power levels of 1.44 MW and 0.73 MW were obtained for maximum and minimum power demand conditions, respectively. On the other hand, the insertion power increases up to 2.0 MW in short feeders of both maximum and minimum power demand conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Radiofrequency Systems and Graphical Interfaces for Industrial Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Currently, graphical user interfaces (GUI) are required that facilitate the interpretation of industrial processes. In this literature, an automatic control system was implemented using a GUI and radio frequency (RF) networks. In addition, the development of the GUI in the Matlab programming and numerical calculation platform is shown. In turn, RF networks certified with Zigbee technology were implemented. For this reason, the Xbee Pro S2 RF module was used in point-to-point networking. Finally, the experimental results obtained from the automatic control system applied to an industrial lighting system are presented.

articleTitle: Unsupervised detection of crop rows from images taken by an unmanned aerial vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This study introduces a methodology for processing high-resolution spatial images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (DAVs) with the goal of detecting crop rows in peri- urban horticultural fields. The image processing approach is unsupervised and solely relies on open-source tools. This ensures that the procedure can be easily generalized and adapted to other datasets with similar features. The article details the sources and attributes of the data used, and outlines the algorithms and concepts involved in the processing journey, culminating in the creation of the final product. The process encompasses the preprocessing of images, field segmentation into individual plots, the rectification and cropping of each plot, and the subsequent detection of crop rows within these plots. The presented methodology holds promise in automating and enhancing the accuracy of crop row detection in horticultural settings, thereby offering invaluable insights for agricultural planning and decision-making.

articleTitle: ISDB- T based Passive Bistatic Radar testbed
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a Passive Bistatic Radar (PBR) testbed that exploits the Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting Terrestrial (ISDB- T) signal, a standard operating in South America and Japan, as an illuminator of opportunity. The system is characterized, and its performance is analyzed. Real experimental results are presented and compared with flight data services, demonstrating the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electromagnetic Field in 132kV Double Circuit Transmission Line using the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This work presents the results of the simulations of the electromagnetic field in the 132 kV transmission line by means of the finite element method using FEMM software. The designs of the structures were exported to the FEMM software to carry out the corresponding simulations of the electromagnetic field emitted by the 132 kV transmission lines for both configurations. As a case study, two types of transmission line configurations currently used by the electric power concessionaire were compared: a)- 1 double three-phase structure, and b)- 2 simple three-phase structures, to determine the values of the electric and magnetic field. The results obtained from the simulations in the FEMM software are evaluated based on what is established by current regulations.

articleTitle: Excitation Reduction to Prevent Stalling in Gensets when Suddenly Loaded
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel strategy to prevent stalling of a genset when subjected to sudden loading. The analysis focuses on the relationship between genset stalling and mechanical dynamics, putting particular attention to the electromagnetic torque and its dependency on the currents flowing through the synchronous generator. Based on this analysis, the goal of this proposal is to prevent stalling by reducing the excitation of the rotor windings, which was shown to work successfully without causing undesired undervoltage. The effectiveness of the strategy proposed is verified through simulations when purely resistive loads are considered.

articleTitle: An automatism for contingency awareness and remediation for power system
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: During the operation of electrical power systems, events can compromise the supply. The Argentine Interconnection System (AIS) has recently suffered adverse events that have led to its collapse. The outcome of these events could have been avoided or limited with properly calibrated automatism and new automatism. There are several types of automatism in the base of the event and the effect that overcomes, in this work the outages lines and the overloads that can occur will be addressed. The paper shows the development and assessment of a special protection scheme (SPS) to avoid protection triggers for overloads of an electrical power system. The performance of the proposed application is tested in a library case and in a real power system case showing improvement in the operational status. Furthermore, the results were tested and validated with professional software for different scenarios and events. Our results demonstrate that the application provides a solid base that can be installed in a Control Center, which allows the operator to run an SPS. This development will be starting point for more sophisticated and extended capabilities for the upcoming challenges for more renewable energy participation.

articleTitle: The Continuous Gabor Transform and Smoothness Analysis of Besicovitch Almost Periodic Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work smoothness analysis of almost-periodic signals is studied. Here, analogously to the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^{2}$</tex> (JR) or finite energy signals, the smoothness of the class of almost periodic bounded power signals is characterized in terms of the decay of its Gabor transform. Moreover, some results are given as equivalence of norms between appropriate function spaces.

articleTitle: Integration of Classification Techniques and Remote Sensing for Periurban Horticulture Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Periurban areas play a crucial role in addressing food security, promoting food sovereignty, and facilitating effective territorial planning. However, there is a lack of comprehensive knowledge and information at the national and regional levels regarding these areas, particularly their land cover and land use patterns, primarily related to local food production systems. This study presents an automated methodology for identifying land cover and land use in twenty-four periurban territories, specifically focusing on differentiating types of vegetables, using remote sensing data from Sentinel 1, 2, and SAOCOM satellite imagery. The accuracy of the developed cartography is validated in teen periurban areas in Argentina, achieving an overall F1 score of > 0.69 for nine land cover and land use classes. Notably, the identification of the horticultural class surpasses an F1 score of > 0.72, indicating promising results in distinguishing various types of vegetables. The ongoing MEPHPRA-PROSAT II project aims to expand the model's capabilities by clustering different periurban areas and ultimately generating 24 comprehensive cartographies that can serve as a foundation for local studies and periodic updates for effective territorial management.

articleTitle: Development of Flexible Capacitors for Energy Harvesting in Smart Packaging
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Supplying power to the sensors and electronic devices that are part of smart packaging is still a challenge. A sustainable solution is through the implementation of energy harvesting systems taking advantage of the RF energy available in the environment. It is proposed to design packaging that is itself an RF wave energy storage and harvesting system. This work focuses on converting the plastic film that makes up the packaging into an energy storage capacitor. Polyethylene nanocomposite films with barium titanate, a material of high dielectric constant, are obtained and their performance as capacitors is analyzed. Fabrication strategies are presented, different titanate loading concentrations are studied and measurements are carried out to demonstrate that it is possible to achieve sufficient capacities to power ultra-low power sensors.

articleTitle: Noise Statistics in Doppler Velocity Estimates of Weather Radars in the Presence of Wi-Fi Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work we present a statistical analysis of the noise component in the Doppler velocity estimates of weather radar applications, when the received signal is affected by Wi-Fi interference. First, expressions for the phase noise that affects the estimates are derived, approximations for these expressions are presented and are established the conditions under which it is valid to apply these approximations. Then, the noise probability density function and its statistical moment are studied. Finally, a series of numerical simulations are conducted that validate the analytical study. These simulations consist in the evaluation of the histogram of the noise and in the estimation of its moments. The results show that interference has a significant effect on the noise statistics even when the interference power with respect to the signal power is not large enough to produce a hop in the velocity estimate.

articleTitle: A Cost-Effective Solution for Characterizing Photonic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Silicon photonics has become an important technology for several applications including high-speed optical communication and optical interconnect, optical sensing, LIDAR, quantum photonics, neural networks, and optical computing and processing. In spite of the maturity of silicon photonics, testing is still troublesome principally because of the difficulty of coupling light into the chips. Although commercial test stations are available, these are pretty expensive for small institutions and companies. We designed and implemented a die-level, semi-automatic, test station. Our solution is capable of testing passive and active photonic components and can be used with the two most common coupling methods, namely, grating couplers and edge couplers.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Filling Missing Pixels in MODIS NDVI Images
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This work focuses on filling missing data in satellite images of the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). Filling missing data in NDVI aims to address the issue of empty pixels in vegetation index maps, which can occur due to various reasons such as lack of satellite information caused by cloud cover. The method presented in this work aims to accurately and coherently reconstruct missing data. The proposed method utilizes interpolation techniques and spatio-temporal analysis to fill gaps in NDVI images.

articleTitle: Validation of a 2D FEM Model for an PMSM with Uniform Pole Demagnetization and Partitioned Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This work presents the experimental validation of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) model with uniform pole demagnetization. Rotor demagnetization may become irreversible if it is not detected early, causing a decrease in torque and performance of PMSM. Uniform pole demagnetization is detected by measuring voltages on half of each phase of an PMSM with partitioned windings. 2D model implemented by the finite element method (FEM) is presented that reproduces the characteristics of a PMSM prototype with modified rotor. Results from the 2D FEM model are presented for the PMSM operating with different uniform demagnetization conditions. Finally, the experimental results obtained in the laboratory validate the simulation signals against different angular speeds and load transients.

articleTitle: Unveiling Argentina's heatwaves: A comprehensive and open analysis of the last 30 years using the ERAS-Land reanalysis product
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Heatwaves are an emerging public concern due to their increasing impacts on global health and economy. The ERAS-Land air temperature product (a freely available reanalysis product from the Copernicus Program), offers a quality controlled and continuous database, which significantly improves the scale and accuracy with respect to point measurements or interpolations between meteorological stations currently used to detect heatwaves in Argentina. In this work we utilized the ERAS-Land product, an open-source software to process 30 years of daily temperature data. We were able to identify the extreme temperature anomalies by calculating the 90th percentile on both minimum and maximum daily temperatures and to determine heatwaves that impacted Argentina over the last 30 years. In addition, a time series clustering algorithm was applied to explore spatio tempo ral patterns of these heatwaves, showing three different patterns along the country. An increasing trend in the number of heatwaves through time was also identified for almost the entire country, with the exception of northwestern Argentina and the coastal areas below the 40° parallel. The results of this work are valuable data that will be used in an environmental epidemiology study along Argentina.

articleTitle: Terrain Subsidence in the Salar de Olaroz (Jujuy, Argentina) Caused by Lithiferous Brine Extraction, Detected by Multi-Temporal SAR Interferometry
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Salar de Olaroz located in the Puna Jujeña is one of the salines in Argentina where several large mining projects of brines extraction for lithium production are concentrated. This activity involves the creation of large drilling parks for pumping underground brine. As the projects have been in production for several years, a multi-temporal SAR interferometry assessment was carried out to detect possible ground subsidence associated with this mining activity. At the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) platform, Sentinel-1 images were processed with the Vertex SBAS tool to generate vertical displacement maps, which resulted in a mapping of cumulative displacements. This leads to detected areas within the salar that show marked patterns of subsidence, concentrated around the drill batteries. The cumulative change values for the period analyzed (2018-2020) range from +12 cm to −17 cm, with an annual rate of progression of between +4 cm to −5 cm, with the maximum subsidence always coinciding with the position of the boreholes. Additionally, control points were used to validate the results, one located within the salar but outside the pumping fields and another which belongs to the IGN's Argentinean high precision geodesic network, where in both the variation measured over time was zero.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Whitening Strategy in the Processing of Argentine Weather Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work, various strategies are implemented to estimate spectral moments from data acquired by Argentine Meteorological Radars. The employed strategies operate on the in-phase and quadrature samples of the range echoes, obtained at a frequency higher than the bandwidth of the transmitted pulse, which determines the range resolution, a condition known as oversampling. In conjunction with the whitening transformation, which allows decorrelating the oversampled signal for each range cell and combining it appropriately, a significant reduction in the variance of the estimates is achieved. This improvement is particularly noticeable when there is a good signal-to-noise ratio relationship.

articleTitle: Designing FPGA-Based Neural Network Models: A Methodological Approach RPIC Estudiantil 2023, 1 al 3 de noviembre de 2023, Oberá, Misiones
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Efficient Neural Networks (NN) are essential in today's data-driven world, due to the ability of solving complex problems, improving efficiency, and automating processes. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) deployment provides a solution to the NN implementation, enabling real time operation and highly scalable systems. This work proposes a methodology to translate pre-trained Floating-Point Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) NN on Fixed-Point MLP NN models, and its implementation with dedicated hardware blocks available on the FPGA, including a performance evaluation of the obtained description by in-circuit debugging tools. This proposal represents a significant savings in NN design and implementation time.

articleTitle: Drought Characterization in Argentina: Relationship Between ENSO Phenomenon and TVDI Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: EI Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon is the relationship between the planet's oceans and atmosphere and their influence on weather and climate. The extreme phases are known as El Niño and La Niña. They can cause prolonged periods of excessive humidity or drought, depending on the region. In Argentina, La Niña phase is considered dry and cold, and El Niño phase is considered wet and warm. However, there is still a lack of understanding of the spatial variability and the impact of each cycle. The Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) is used for the characterization of ENSO strength and intensity, while the Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) can be used for the characterization of soil-plant moisture status. In this study, the relationship between the ONI index and the TVDI anomalies during spring (September-November) and summer (December-February) was analyzed. This was done for the period 2000–2022. The whole surface of Argentina was studied. The results show that a large part of the agricultural area in the center and east of Argentina was affected by drought during La Niña phases in summer, while the west and east of the country were affected in spring.

articleTitle: Web-Based SCADA System to Control and Monitor Electrical Grids’ Distribution Transformers and Medium Voltage Reclosers, Based on IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This project focuses on developing communication devices for data acquisition and control in distribution transformers' energy meters and reclosers in urban and rural Electrical Grids in Morteros, Córdoba, aiming to stremline operational efficiency and decision-making during emergencies. Specifically, an IoT ecosystem is proposed using ESP32 microcontrollers to periodically read energy meters at substations, interpreting the DLMS COSEM protocol. Additionally, remote control and data acquisition of reclosers are targeted by decoding the DNP3 protocol. After implementation and several months of operation, the project concludes favorably, since monitoring and control of the targeted equipment was achieved, allowing early alerting in case of failures and serving as a future tool to enhance the electrical grid's management through AI algorithms or optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Novel method for measuring and processing field spectral data for water quality applications
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: The accelerated eutrophication of water bodies is a global problem and requires monitoring with high spatial and temporal resolution. Satellite remote sensing techniques have proven to be useful to detect and quantify an indicator of this phenomenon, chlorophyll-a concentration, where the associated error propagation is crucial to understand these data. This work presents a novel method for measuring and processing field spectral data for water quality applications with a special focus on statistical uncertainties. The radiometric data obtained from San Roque reservoir in Cordoba, Argentina, was processed using a bootstrap algorithm to obtain the mean reflectance and its standard deviation. The proposed algorithm includes flagging of unfavorable water reflectance measurements due to sky conditions and floating algae, as well as remnant sunglint correction using the reflectance of the 1350 nm. The results showed that the proposed algorithm improved the accuracy of radiometric data by reducing the standard deviation and the remnant sunglint effect. Linear regression analysis showed a higher correlation between the measured reflectances with total and water quality variables for the new method. The proposed algorithm yielded smaller prediction errors for total chlorophyll and turbidity compared to the current algorithm by a factor of 1.9 ± 0.2 and 3.7 ± 0.3.

articleTitle: Implementation of a 10 Gbps Coherent Receiver for Free-Space Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: We show the implementation of an optical coherent receiver suitable for inter-satellite communications supporting both Dual-Polarization Binary Phase Shift Keying (DP-BPSK) and Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (DP-QPSK) modulation formats, enabling data transmission at rates of up to 10 Gbps. The performance of the implemented receiver's digital signal processing algorithms is numerically and experimentally evaluated under different operation conditions and channel impairments, such as received power, carrier frequency offset, laser linewidth, and polarization rotation.

articleTitle: Full Spectrum for Rotating Electrical Machines Condition Monitoring and Fault Diagnosis: a Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: The full spectrum is a widely used technique for condition monitoring and fault diagnosis in rotating electrical machines. However, it is known under different names and approaches to analyse both vibration and electrical measurements. The full spectrum allows simultaneous quadrature analysis of periodic signals. For each frequency component of the signals, a direct sequence or positive component and an inverse sequence or negative component can be obtained. In this work, a general and unified description of the full spectrum is carried out. Moreover, the main applications for fault diagnosis through vibration and current analysis are described. Experimental results obtained on the same induction motor are shown to analyse the differences and similarities between the full spectrum of vibrations and electrical variables.

articleTitle: Control-aware Co-Design of A Wave Energy Converter for the Argentine Sea Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Despite the favourable energy conditions in the Argentine sea (South Atlantic Ocean), the country has not yet actively participated in the development and utilisation of wave energy resources. Control co-design (CCD) is a novel control- aware design paradigm that integrates the energy-maximising control from early stages of system design, allowing for optimisation driven by the considered control strategy to achieve an overall optimal design. In this study, considering an overall control-aware design perspective, a wave energy converter system is specifically tailored for the Argentine sea conditions, analysing different WEC structural configurations (geometry and dimensions). The performance of different control structures, including a spectral-based control methodology and a reactive controller, are assessed for each configuration. Realistic operating conditions, specifically tailored to the ocean wave modes prevalent in the Argentine sea, are taken into account during the performance analysis. The results obtained from the study are thoroughly discussed, highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of the considered control strategies in the context of the Argentine sea.

articleTitle: Approximating the solution of an Economic MPC using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Economic model predictive control is a recognized advanced control strategy which calculates control actions by solving an optimization problem in real time. The issue of numerical computation is the main barrier to implementing this type of controller. Deep learning has emerged as a promising solution to reduce the computational cost. This paper proposes a deep learning approximation of an Economic MPC, particularly with artificial neural networks, of the control strategy for managing energy resources in a residential microgrid. Operational data were generated from the solution established by the controller to train, validate and test the neural network using Matlab. Simulation results showed that the proposed approach can approximate the control strategy correctly.

articleTitle: Comparison between Air Temperature and different Land Surface Temperature satellite products for the City of Córdoba, Argentina
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In the current context of climate change, the use of remote sensing in urban applications such as Urban Heat Islands risk mapping, provides valuable and timely information to address this challenge. By better understanding their environment and impacts, cities can work towards a more sustainable and resilient future. In recent years, platforms and code processors such as Google Earth Engine (GEE) have offered the possibility to visualize and work with different geoprocessed ready-to-use data. Land surface temperature (LST) is one of those products and it is a key parameter in the physics of land surface processes on regional and global scales. However, it is necessary to assess their performance before using them for studies such as social vulnerability, resilience, and risk management. In this study, different medium and high spatial resolution satellite products available in GEE were compared with 3-year data of 10 meteorological stations strategically located in the Metropolitan Area of Córdoba city, Argentina. The time series were compared using different statistical parameters, in which linear regressions were used and compared with a train and validated semi-empirical model. The results indicate that the predictive model outperforms the original LST data for all LST products analyzed. Thus, it is advisable to adjust the model before using the satellite-ready-to-use product.

articleTitle: “Temporal Analysis of Precipitation in the Lower and Middle Paraguay Basin within the La Plata Basin (2001-2020) and its Relationship with the El Niño/Southern Oscillation (ENSO) Phenomenon”
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this work, a time-dependent analysis is presented to identify climatic patterns that affect precipitation behavior in the lower and middle Paraguay River basin, corresponding to the territory of Paraguay. For this purpose, satellite precipitation images were used for the period from 2001 to 2020, available on the GIOVANNI - NASA platform. The results of the exploratory analysis of classical statistics allowed the identification of data distribution, probability density, and monthly, seasonal, and annual statistical measures. It was observed that the monthly average precipitation of the time series reaches a maximum in August 2015 (312.4 mm) and a minimum in August 2004 (6.5 mm). It was determined that December is the month with the highest monthly average precipitation in the series, while August has the lowest precipitation. On the other hand, stochastic models were applied to identify and evaluate the possibility of generating precipitation forecasts using the autoregressive ARIMA model, with unsatisfactory results because the series does not meet the necessary assumptions for the implementation of these models. A Fourier analysis was performed to detect periods of high and low flow, clearly identifying characteristic or dominant frequencies related to cycles of 1, 4, 5, 20, 10, and 0.5 years. The application of this technique allowed relating the occurrence of anomalies in the flows to hydroclimatic cycles during the two phases of the El Niño/Southern Oscillation (ENSO) phenomenon that occur in tropical South America, including Paraguay, among other countrie). The space image analysis identified the accumulation of the monthly average precipitation over 20 years, alternating between areas of Low Chaco with low precipitation (47 mm) and others with higher (332 mm) towards the east and center of the basin. Finally, Voronoi (Thiessen) interpolation was performed using monthly average precipitation data from the stations and the Isoyetas map, allowing visualization of precipitation patterns in the studied area.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Two Adaptive Predictive Control Strategies to be Implemented in Artificial Pancreas Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This work presents a comparative study of two control algorithms based on specific characteristics of innovative adaptive predictive control. One of them consists on including in the algorithm a set of rules to choose between two alternatives: Adaptive Predictive part and a Robust Filter (APCwRF). This last version was called enhanced (E) APCwRF. The second methodology is the Predictive Functional Control (PFC) where the parameters of its internal model are continuously adapted to follow the real patient evolution by a recursive estimation based on UD factorization. This last option was called “adaptive PFC (APFC)”. The main objective of both strategies is to provide improvements to the Artificial Pancreas (AP) technology for patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) disease. The EAPCwRF can be implemented with two alternative models the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) and the nonlinear Wiener-type block-oriented. In both cases the model parameters are updated by performing recursive identification using a Kalman Filter (KF). Hence, the control algorithm checks the quality of the prediction of the two options (FIR and Wiener) and decides which of them is more adequate to be adopted. The robust filter part is able to choose between the two models to be implemented. The tests are performed with four strategies: APCwRF, EAPCwRF, PFC and APFC together with real data of the patient without control. We used a previously developed global data-driven model (GM) for defining the final tuning (commissioning). The closed loop responses are tested with the in silico patient obtained through dynamic simulations of the GM for different meals intake and insulin dosages. The new strategies, EAPCwRF and APFC, included the insulin pump shut down when the GM predicts hypoglycemic events and exceed the recommended insulin on board (IOB) magnitude for the patient N° 5041 from the Center of Diabetes Technology (UVa/USA). The Control Variability Grid Analysis (CVGA) and the percentage of time with the patient inside the healthy range are considered to evaluate the control algorithm performances. Based on them, we present the conclusions and discuss some future works.

Author Keywords: robust filter global data driven models

articleTitle: Mitigation of WiFi Interference in Velocity Estimation for Staggered-PRT Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In this paper we analyse the effect of interference from WiFi network transmissions on the Doppler velocity estimates of C-band weather radars using the Staggered Pulse Repetition Time (SPRT) mode, and we propose a method to mitigate this effect. Starting from a simplified signal model, we obtain closed form expressions of how interference affects two of the simplest and most widely used estimation methods, from which we derive our proposal. Through numerical simulations we analyze the performance of the different methods when using this simplified model and a more realistic and accepted signal model for the meteorological target. The proposed method achieves performance improvement for low Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR), both in conditions without interference and with moderate interference.

articleTitle: Heuristic Approach for Production Planning in Agro-Industrial SMEs
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper presents the advances related to the activities carried out in an agro-industrial SME in Rafaela, Argentina. The company specializes in the commercialization of gearboxes for agricultural machinery, as well as component parts for such gearboxes as spare parts. Currently, the company lacks a planning system that allows it to organize its operations, resulting in non-compliance with agreed delivery dates (with associated costs). This paper presents an initial approach to the operations management problem (i.e., purchasing management, stock management, supplier selection, and production planning), which involves the development of a mathematical programming model. The constraints integrated into the model arise from the actual needs of the company, addressing the issue of shortages in a general sense (late deliveries of gearboxes and lost sales of component parts as spares). The objective is to define the policies to be followed in the next quarter in a way that minimizes component acquisition costs, maintains appropriate stock levels (both for gearboxes and components), and minimizes late deliveries to customers. As for the preliminary results obtained, the model was tested with a subset of products and compared with the available sales history. The results were promising: the historical operations, without a decision support tool, had less than 30 % on-time delivery (meaning that over 70 % of deliveries were made after the agreed-upon date), while the solution proposed by the model resulted in 98 % on-time deliveries, with proper management of component parts stock.

articleTitle: Estimation of Mutual Information between Pairs of Biomechanical Signals with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This research showcases the utilization of MINE (Mutual Information Neural Estimator) to assess mutual information between biomechanical signals, specifically focusing on the relationship between toe height and knee angles during the normal walking patterns of healthy individuals. Through simulated data trials, it was determined that the most effective network design consisted of three layers with 50 units each, using ReLU activation functions. Consequently, we developed an approach to examine the mutual information between toe height and knee joint angles, which resulted in two notable outcomes: consistent estimations and agreement with evaluated gait cycles. During the swing phase, there was a higher degree of mutual information between toe height and same-side knee angles as compared to contralateral knee angles, indicating a stronger predictive relationship between toe height and collateral knee angles. Conversely, in the stance phase, mutual information values were nearly zero regardless of knee angle side - an anticipated result since foot height remains constant while knee angles change. Evaluating the entire gait cycle revealed a pattern resembling that of the swing phase, though with differing mutual information values, suggesting an interdependence between the swing and stance phases. In conclusion, MINE proves to be reliable across various hyperparameter configurations. The proposed methodology presents a proficient and precise means for examining complex correlations within biomedical data, holding potential for customized rehabilitation plans and varied biomedical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Microbial Fuel Cell fed with a substrate of slow biodegradability
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) degrade organic matter through the activity of electroactive microorganisms. The significance lies in utilizing organic waste, particularly digestate waste, due to its complex organic substrate of slow biodegradability. Given the considerable interest in this process, a model that represents the dynamics of these substrates and their correlation with the current production, is presented. The model encompasses the hydrolysis and diffusion stages in the biofilm of a slowly biodegradable organic matter component. The electroactive bacteria's activity induces hydrolysis, transforming it into rapidly biodegradable organic matter and subsequently into a flow of electrons delivered to the anode. The model comprises ten differential equations describing the behavior of the slowly biodegradable organic matter component and the rapidly biodegradable matter in the biofilm layers, a differential equation representing the charge accumulation in the biofilm, and the non-linear Buttler-Volmer equation. An identification procedure was undertaken to determine the values of the nine parameters utilized in the model. Subsequently, an experimental validation of the model was conducted, demonstrating its successful representation of the behavior of the MFC when fed with the digestate.

articleTitle: Phase Amplitude Coupling Workflow for Mapping EEG Signals to Standard Brain Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Human brain mapping or neuroimaging plays a pivotal role in understanding the intricacies of the human brain and paving the way for potential therapeutic interventions. Studying the standard brain networks, typically obtained from fMRI, provide valuable insights into the fundamental organization of the human brain. In this work we present a workflow for processing electroencephalography (EEG) signals to determine the correlations of the phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) of the standard brain networks during a given time-window. We validate this pipeline with synthetic signals on realistic head models of two subjects with the ultimate goal of studying the changes of these networks during different sleep stages. The proposed workflow consists of: mapping the signals to the source space, averaging per Brodmann Area (BA), low and high pass filtering, computing the modulation index per low-high frequency pair, generating surrogate data to obtain significance thresholds, obtaining the significant PAC signals, computing the signal and noise covariance matrices, removing the model bias, and applying confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to determine the relevance of each standard brain network. We included the novelty of using CFA instead of principal component analysis as done in previous studies. We tested the workflow with synthetic signals, and it performed as expected. Next steps will be fine-tuning it and improving its robustness before processing real signals during sleep that we already have collected for the two subjects of the head models used here.

articleTitle: Connecting sensitivity, identifiability and interpretability of a glucose minimal model
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Mathematical models have increased their applications in physiology, control and systems science, and biomedical engineering because they offer the opportunity to examine the structure and behavior of complex physiological systems. In addition, they provide a concise description of complex dynamic processes, indicating ways to improve experimental design and allowing the testing of hypotheses related to physiological structure. When building a mathematical model, it is important to assess the impact of different factors on the overall behavior of the system being modeled and to determine which variables have the most significant influence on the system. Properties such as identifiability, sensitivity, and interpretability in mathematical models are crucial for representing real-world phenomena. In this paper, a sensitivity, structural identifiability, and qualitative parameter interpretability analysis is carried out in a new version of the minimal model of the glucose-insulin system proposed by Bergman. The aim was to evaluate the structure of this new mathematical model and the existing relationship among sensitivity, identifiability, and interpretability of the model parameters. The findings demonstrated the connection between the properties of sensitivity, structural identifiability, and parameter interpretability, which provide important details about the model structure.

articleTitle: Qualitative Estimation of Sun-Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence (SIF) Using Sentinel-3 OLCI Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper evaluates the ability of Sentinel-3 satellite data to qualitatively estimate chlorophyll fluorescence, a direct indicator of the physiological state of vegetation. Estimates are compared in absorption zones, O2-B and O2-A, using data collected in three different ecosystems. The proposed method calculates the simple ratio of radiance outside and inside the oxygen absorption bands. Results show that the method, using the O2-A absorption band, can effectively predict field-derived chlorophyll fluorescence measurements. The observed differences between the variants are discussed and the importance of considering errors and biases in the measurements is pointed out. This qualitative approach based on satellite data offers potential for improving spatial and temporal resolution in monitoring chlorophyll fluorescence at global or regional scales.

articleTitle: Understanding Interpretability in Modeling Biotechnological Processes: A Critical Review
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In the field of process engineering, mathematical models play a fundamental role in better understanding systems and developing model-based systems for decision-making. These models are representations used to capture the key features of a system or process for a specific purpose, such as knowledge generation, estimation, control, optimization, and others. However, the validity of these models depends in some cases on the scope defined by the applicable theory, law, or principles, the experimental dataset used for their development and validation, as well as on the ability of these models to interact with their end users. In this sense, interpretability is an essential property that determines to what extent a human operator can interpret the model. However, the definition of this property is not clear, as there is no consensus on the concept in the literature. In this paper, we provide a state-of-the-art review of the various definitions of interpretability available in the literature as well as a critical analysis of the lack of uniqueness of the interpretability concept for the mathematical modeling spectrum, specifically in applications associated with biotechnological processes. This work is not an exhaustive study of the literature, but rather an approach to the existing differences between the definitions of interpretability and a proposal for the generalization of the concept.

articleTitle: Spatial analysis of factors linked to Community Food Environments in argentine urban localities, during 2018-2019
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: In Argentina, food environments and health aspects related to them, such as low birth weight (lbw) and macrosomia, have not yet been studied using geoscience tools at a regional scale. This work aims to spatially describe the distribution of birth weight and associated food environment variables in Argentina during the 2018-2019 period. Methods: using open data, the prevalence of lbw and macrosomia was characterized for the period 2018-2019, in 657 urban localities in Argentina (>5000 inhabitants). Based on the community food environments model, socioeconomic, demographic, and environmental variables (from remote sensing) were characterized, which were grouped into three environment dimensions: policy, environmental, and individual. A description of the spatial distribution of each variable was conducted. An optimized hot spot analysis (arcgis pro 3.1) and a purely spatial analysis (satscan) were carried out. Cartography was processed with qgis 3.22. Results: low-risk clusters for lbw and macrosomia were observed in places with lower food insecurity, altitude, proportion of households with unsatisfied basic needs (ubn), and higher percentage of social security coverage. High-risk clusters for lbw coincide with areas of lower food insecurity, infant mortality rate, percentage of households with female headship, ubn, and higher altitude and social security coverage. Furthermore, a high-risk cluster for macrosomia was observed in areas with higher food insecurity, vegetation index, precipitation, percentage of households with ubn, and lower social security coverage. Discussion: it is important to study the spatial behavior of environment variables before conducting explanatory or predictive modeling, as these often render the spatial relationships between them invisible.

articleTitle: Development of a crop extension product in Argentina using MODIS data at 250m and NDVI thresholds estimated from phenological metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Agriculture is an economic activity of great importance in the Argentine Republic due to its extensive arable land, favourable climatic conditions and agricultural tradition. In order to plan and manage land use effectively, it is essential to know the location and extent of the areas dedicated to annual summer cropping in each agricultural season. In this study, a map of the areas dedicated to extensive annual summer cropping has been produced with a spatial resolution of 250 metres, covering a large area that includes 14 Argentine provinces. The methodology used was based on multi-temporal NDVI data from MODIS and field reference records of soybean and maize crops. NDVI temporal signatures of the crop growth cycle were analysed and NDVI thresholds for the phenological stages of ‘emergence’, ‘flowering’ and ‘physiological maturity’ were calculated. These thresholds were used to create decision rules to be applied to a series of NDVI images from the MOD13Q1 product (period 2000-2021) in order to map areas for annual agricultural use. The results showed the technical feasibility of identifying areas dedicated to the production of annual summer crops. One map was obtained for each agricultural campaign analysed. The maps showed an increase in the area dedicated to agriculture over the period 2000-2021. Comparing the area mapped by campaign with the areas estimated by the National Agriculture Agency, a very good agreement between the values was observed throughout the period. When the 2010-2021 maps were evaluated with the ground reference data, the overall accuracy was around 52-72%. The present maps are an unpublished product in the Argentine Republic, they show good validation values and can be very useful for subsequent studies.

articleTitle: A Fast Pseudorandom Number Generator Residue Number System Based
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: This paper presents the construction of a high throughput pseudorandom number generator circuit with a uniform distribution density function, based on the residue number system. The use of the Residue Number System allows the generation of random numbers of a large number of bits at high speed. The proposed generator is subjected to a series of basic statistical studies, the Diehard test, complexity test, and calculation of the Hurst exponent, in order to validate the random quality of the generated sequences. Results of this study are compared with an ideal generator and others, which are taken as reference.

articleTitle: Network traffic modeled on path dependent queues
publicationTitle: 2023 XX Workshop on Information Processing and Control (RPIC)
abstract: Network traffic modeled as queues where the probability of a new entry depends on the history of the arrival process is analyzed. Based on this characteristic, we propose to use the generalized Polya stochastic processes (GPPs). The theoretical background of such type of queue is reviewed and the heavy-tailed epochs property is shown to hold for the arrival rates we consider. The probability of instability or congestion for the GPP/M/1 and GPP/GPP/1 queues is analyzed from simulations. The results agree with theoretical results for the Polya process, and show interesting similarities and differences when a recently proposed arrival rate distinct from that of Polya is used. Simulation results and possible further directions are discussed.
